text:
Riley (AE): Quick heads-up: ACME needs a presales package by EOD tomorrow. They asked for reserved GPU sizing, autoscale policy, preheat/KV warmup steps, fallback routing to cheaper model when latency or cost thresholds hit, and security checklist answers (KMS, VPC peering, audit retention). Traffic profile: steady 200 RPS, ad-hoc 1-min spikes to 1,200 RPS, median 30 tokens per req. Primary: llama2-70b-q4 (H100), fallback: redwood-rl-13b (~A10G), embeddings: tiny-embed. They want a hard monthly cost cap and automatic downgrade when P95 > 300ms. Can we rapid-fire confirm feasibility?

Sam (Solutions): Clarify: 200 RPS is requests/sec, right? And spikes are unpredictable (marketing-driven)? Also do they require 99th latency SLAs during spikes or just best-effort?

Riley (AE): Yes requests/sec. Spikes are ad-hoc. They emphasized P99 during spikes but will settle for a documented fallback for production.

Arjun (Infra): Ballpark perf: with our H100 config and batching, one optimized serving pod handles ~80-120 RPS for 30-token median. Baseline 200 RPS -> reserve 2 pods (3 preferred for headroom). For 1,200 RPS spikes -> ~10-12 pods. Recommend reserved pool of 3 H100 pods + 2 A10G for embeddings/fallback routing. Burst/autoscale should allow adding up to 9 H100 pods on demand (spot where acceptable) with routing to redwood-rl-13b if capacity unavailable.

Maya (PM): From product: cost levers are quantization and routing. If q4_k variant can preserve quality we could drop ~15-25% capacity. Suggest Optimize run to validate. Also policy: if P95 > 300ms for >15s, trigger new-traffic route to redwood-rl-13b-q4_k; keep existing in-flight completions on primary.

Sam (Solutions): Autoscale policy sketch: min_nodes = cover 200 RPS baseline (reserve), max_nodes = baseline + 9 burst, scale_up_cooldown = 30s, scale_down_cooldown = 120s. Burst pool uses pre-negotiated burst credits for committed customers; otherwise PAYG. Provide JSON example in presales packet.

Arjun (Infra): Preheat/KV warmup: run rolling preheat per-AZ, exercise top 50 prompts, prime KV cache snapshot on deploy. Secrets rotations: rotating control-plane KMS keys triggers redeploy for control-plane components but doesn't invalidate KV entries; still plan re-warm after rotation. Recommend scheduling rotation off-peak.

Beth (Security): KMS + customer-managed HSM supported. VPC peering & private control plane supported; we deliver audit logs to chosen S3 bucket and CloudWatch. Need to confirm EU residency and audit retention length. Also note: for private deployments, we can offer longer retention as an add-on.

Riley (AE): ACME wants EU residency (eu-west-1) and 12 months audit retention. Also asked whether fallback routing is auditable per request.

Beth (Security): Yes, we log routing decisions and model variants per request in audit trail; include sample log schema in answers. Will prepare security bundle with KMS, VPC peering steps, audit retention options.

Sam (Solutions): Pricing sketch for presales (order of magnitude):
- Committed reserved: 3 H100 + 2 A10G reserved + burst credits -> ~$72k - $95k / month depending on term and region.
- PAYG equivalent covering same traffic -> ~$110k - $140k / month.
Recommend presenting both a committed plan (with cost cap + burst credits) and a capped fallback plan where model-routing enforces the cap.

Maya (PM): Actionable: run a quick Optimize quantization check on llama2-70b to estimate capacity savings. If q4_k holds, we can reduce reserved nodes by ~20%. I'll try to run a lightweight eval and report back.

Arjun (Infra): I'll generate a one-page sizing calc with conservative and aggressive variants: node counts, expected RPS per pod, memory/KV warm requirements, and warmup steps. ETA 3pm PT.

Sam (Solutions): I'll draft the autoscale + fallback policy and include a JSON policy example and SLA blurb for reserved pools (recommended 90% uptime credit tiers). ETA 2pm PT.

Beth (Security): I'll assemble the security answers (KMS, VPC peering, audit logs sample, data residency confirmation) and note retention options. ETA 4pm PT.

Maya (PM): I'll produce the Optimize estimate and recommended A/B canary parameters (5% traffic, 10m). ETA 5pm PT best effort.

Riley (AE): I'll assemble the presales packet: 1) reserved config + pricing range, 2) autoscale + fallback policy, 3) security notes confirming EU region + 12-month retention, 4) canary + preheat plan. Target: send to ACME by EOD and schedule 9am ET presales call tomorrow.

deploy-bot: Note: eu-west-1 spot capacity available for burst pools; may be preemptible. No open incidents.

Riley (AE): One more ask: include a short paragraph on how fallback affects SLOs and customer experience (e.g., quality tradeoff matrix). Sam/Maya please include.

Sam (Solutions): Will add a cost vs latency vs quality matrix and SLA impacts.

Riley (AE): Thanks everyone, closing thread after attachments are ready.

(End of thread)
